text:
meera: Heads-up — we just hit a weird billing/attribution gap in staging. A request from a project-scoped API key fell back to the shared pool and the billing row shows the shared pool key, not the originating project. Can we make the telemetry show both origin and effective key?

alex: ugh. yeah that's been annoying. I think we only log the final routed key id in the request envelope. We should include origin_key_id and fallback_reason.

sam: +1. also want to know which routing policy triggered the fallback (e.g., capacity/ quota/region). otherwise it's hard to debug customer reports.

meera: Exactly. Customer complained their per-project quota didn't decrement (because it used shared pool), so they saw unexpected billing charges and no quota consumption.

alex: Quick proposal: add telemetry fields: origin_key_id, origin_org_id, routed_key_id, routed_pool, fallback_reason, routing_policy. Example event:
```json
{
  "event": "request_routed",
  "origin_key_id": "key_abc",
  "origin_project": "proj-42",
  "routed_key_id": "pool_shared_1",
  "routed_pool": "shared-v2",
  "fallback_reason": "quota_exhausted",
  "routing_policy": "capacity-first",
  "latency_ms": 123
}
```

maya: that JSON looks good. Are we concerned about PII/PII-like leakage? origin_org_id might be sensitive depending on export rules. Need to gate in logs/exports.

sam: we should definitely redact org/project in aggregated telemetry exports but keep full IDs in internal traces (retained for 7d). Also add a boolean "origin_claimed" to indicate whether the origin attribution should drive billing/quota.

meera: How would console surface this? We should show route history per request in traces tab and add an attribution badge in billing UI when routed_key_id != origin_key_id.

alex: UX idea: show a small pill: "Routed: shared-v2 (fallback: quota) — billed to Org X" with a link to the trace. Default collapsed. We can iterate.

infra-bot: deploy queued: telemetry-schema v2 -> staging at 2025-11-03T14:02Z (meera/infra).

meera: I'll own schema PR. Implementation notes: runtime needs to populate origin_* from auth layer before routing, and routing layer must append routed_* and fallback_reason. Also ensure header names don't collide with existing x-rw- headers.

sam: small nit: some requests come from service accounts that intentionally want to be routed to org pooled capacity (billing separate). We need an opt-out flag on the key: "disable_origin_attribution": true to honor billing intent.

alex: good call. We'll add that to key metadata. Default false. If true, origin fields are still recorded for auditing but not used for billing attribution.

meera: timeline? If infra-bot is queuing, can we get a staging run today and a canary for console next week?

infra-bot: deployment started to staging. Tests: unit + e2e + telemetry smoke. ETA 45m.

maya: When we expose to analytics exports (e.g., data warehouse), include routed_pool but drop origin_project/org unless flagged by compliance. We'll need a config in the export pipeline.

sam: Implementation checklist I'll take:
- add schema fields in telemetry (meera)
- auth layer: attach origin metadata (alex)
- routing: append routed metadata + fallback_reason (sam)
- key metadata flag for disable_origin_attribution (meera)
- console: trace UI + billing pill design (maya)
- data exports: redaction rules (maya)

meera: I'll open PRs and link here. Thanks.

alex: thanks, will sync after staging pass.

meera: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/pulls/1428 — includes schema, unit tests.

infra-bot: staging deployment succeeded: telemetry-schema v2 -> staging (2025-11-03T14:46Z).

sam: ✅ verified fields in staging traces for a simulated fallback. origin_key_id present, routed_pool present, fallback_reason=quota_exhausted. Console design pass scheduled for Tue.

meera: closing loop: plan to roll to canary next week, then global. Keep an eye on storage costs (more fields) and retention.

maya: noted — will coordinate with analytics for redaction and docs for customers.
